DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter Disease

Since the pain is localized to the tibial tubercle and X-rays are normal, this fits the classic presentation of Osgood-Schlatter disease in an active 7-year-old male, especially given the absence of infection markers and trauma. The diagnosis is confirmed by the characteristic pain at the knee's front, below the kneecap, which worsens with activity. I recommend observing the child and avoiding high-impact sports for now to allow the bone to catch up with growth.
